item.title: Anthropic to add US voting information to Claude before midterms
item.description: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms. The AI company said its goal was to position Claude as a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. "Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app," the company said in a statement, citing analysis of 250,000 US conversations. The move comes as AI companies increasingly position chatbots as sources of news and information, potentially helping Anthropic draw more users during the election cycle. About 0.51% of Claude conversations are specifically about elections or voting, Anthropic said, adding that it expects political and election-related queries to rise as election day approaches. Later this month, US users seeking voting logistics will receive answers drawn directly from Democracy Works’ database of state and local election sources. Anthropic said requests for recommendations on how to vote were extremely rare, accounting for just 0.01% of U.S. conversations.

item.title: NLCS resale ticket prices plummet 42% with Dodgers facing 0-2 hole
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers' losses in the first two games of the National League Championship Series are having an impact on resale ticket prices at Dodger Stadium.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Dodgers' losses in the first two games of the National League Championship Series are having an impact on resale ticket prices at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers find themselves trailing in the best-of-seven series against the Milwaukee Brewers, with games set for Wednesday and Thursday in Los Angeles. As of early Wednesday, the get-in price (including fees) on the resale market for Game 3 had fallen in three days by 42% from $167 on Sunday night to $97 per ticket, according to TicketData. Game 4 tickets were down 37% to $98. Los Angeles led MLB in attendance for the 13th straight season with a total of 4.03 million to set a franchise record. There were 14 sellouts and 40 crowds of more than 50,000 at Dodger Stadium, the largest MLB ballpark (capacity 56,000). The average for 81 games was 49,805. While the Dodgers are trying to become the first team to win three consecutive World Series in 26 years, the Brewers are on track to reach their first World Series since 1982 -- when they were in the American League. Resale tickets for a potential World Series Game 1 in Milwaukee at American Family Field (capacity 41,900) was at $1,122 per ticket, up 2% since Monday, per TicketData. --Field Level Media

item.title: Perella Weinberg, Piper Sandler abandon merger talks, source says
item.description: Investment bank Piper Sandler and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger as they could not agree on financial and personnel terms, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Abigail Summerville
item.content:encoded: Investment bank Piper Sandler (PIPR.N) and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners (PWP.O) have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger as they could not agree on financial and personnel terms, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday. Shares of Perella Weinberg closed 19.1% lower at $13, while those of Piper Sandler ended up 0.96% at $64.5. Perella Weinberg declined to comment, while Piper Sandler did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Financial Times first reported on Wednesday that the merger talks fell through. The Wall Street Journal had reported last month that Piper Sandler was in talks to buy Perella Weinberg, which had a market value of about $1.4 billion at the time. A $485-million merger between Minneapolis-based Piper Jaffray and New York-based Sandler O'Neill led to the formation of Piper Sandler Companies in January 2020, creating a major investment bank specializing in the middle market, with leading advisory practices in financial services, healthcare and energy. Meanwhile, Perella Weinberg was founded by veteran Wall Street bankers Joseph Perella, Peter Weinberg and Terry Meguid in 2006. The firm went public in 2021 through a merger with a blank-check company backed by banking entrepreneur Betsy Cohen, in a deal valued at about $975 million.

item.title: Alza del IPC agudiza caída de las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial
item.description: Las principales acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial se desplomaban el miércoles tras la publicación del más reciente informe sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos, lo que puso de manifiesto la preocupación de los inversionistas por los riesgos que plantea el aumento de los costos financieros en un sector que requiere un gran volumen de capital.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Darshan R, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: Las principales acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial se desplomaban el miércoles tras la publicación del más reciente informe sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos, lo que puso de manifiesto la preocupación de los inversionistas por los riesgos que plantea el aumento de los costos financieros en un sector que requiere un gran volumen de capital. Entre las empresas que más caían, el operador de centros de datos CoreWeave (CRWV.O) bajaba un 16%; el proveedor de infraestructura de IA Nebius (NBIS.O) retrocedía un 11%; el gigante de la computación en la nube Oracle (ORCL.N) se desplomaba un 9%; y el fabricante de servidores Dell Technologies (DELL.N) se hundía un 11%. Los descensos sumaban una pérdida de valor de mercado de 80.000 millones de dólares. Las caídas reflejan el impacto de un endurecimiento de las condiciones financieras, así como las ganancias desmesuradas obtenidas por algunos de los principales beneficiarios del auge de la IA. Barclays bajó el miércoles la recomendación para Dell y otras dos compañías de hardware empresarial, señalando que las acciones de Dell se han cuadruplicado este año por la fiebre inversora impulsada por la IA, la que ha provocado que 16 títulos del sector tecnológico del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) se hayan, como mínimo, duplicado este año, según cálculos de Reuters. La preocupación por el aumento de los costos de financiación también lastraba a otras empresas el miércoles. El desplome era particularmente intenso en el caso de CoreWeave, que ha emitido 22.000 millones de dólares en bonos y ha tomado préstamos por 26.000 millones, según datos de LSEG. El bono de CoreWeave emitido en junio con un rendimiento del 9,625% ofrecía recientemente un retorno del 15%. "Estamos recibiendo mucha información que sugiere que las mayores empresas de IA podrían no estar generando los beneficios o los ingresos que se esperaban, y creo que eso hace que todo el mundo se sienta nervioso respecto a empresas como CoreWeave", dijo Kim Forrest, directora de inversiones de Bokeh Capital Partners. El presidente ejecutivo de CoreWeave, Mike Intrator, dijo en un memorándum interno que el mercado está actuando de forma "irracional" y que sigue confiando en la empresa de IA en la nube, informó Bloomberg el miércoles. La caída del miércoles es la más reciente señal de un mercado que lucha por asimilar las implicaciones de la alta inflación, en un momento en el que el endeudamiento corporativo impulsado por la IA ha contribuido a elevar las tasas de interés en el mundo. En general, los inversionistas siguen mostrándose optimistas respecto al sector, en parte porque sus principales actores, desde el fabricante de chips Nvidia (NVDA.O) hasta los denominados "hiperescaladores" (principalmente Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) y Amazon (AMZN.O) ), son muy rentables y se considera que están bien gestionados, a pesar de la preocupación por su endeudamiento. Sin embargo, el aumento de las tasas de interés encarecerá el financiamiento y la construcción, un hecho que probablemente afectará en primer lugar a las empresas no rentables y a las menos rentables. "Creo que unas tasas de largo plazo sobre el 5% y que se acercan sigilosamente al 6% suponen un problema para lo que yo llamaría los prestatarios marginales", dijo Ross Mayfield, analista de estrategia de inversión de Baird, en una entrevista con Reuters. "Se complica mucho más la situación para las empresas que se sitúan por debajo de las cuatro grandes hiperescaladoras". El índice Nasdaq (.IXIC) bajaba un 2% el miércoles por la tarde, con Alphabet y el resto de grandes hiperescaladoras con caídas de alrededor del 2%. SpaceX (SPCX.O) , otra importante empresa del sector de la IA, perdía un 3%. "Supongo que ahora el grupo ha crecido hasta cinco. SpaceX se ha sumado a la fiesta para unirse a Meta, Microsoft, Google y Amazon", dijo Jed Ellerbroek, gestor de carteras de Argent Capital Management. "Las cinco empresas están gastando alrededor del 75% del dinero que se invierte en centros de datos en el país (Estados Unidos). Y, obviamente, están destinando todas sus ganancias, e incluso algo más, a estos centros de datos, y la rentabilidad que obtienen de ellos es realmente buena".

item.title: Delantero mexicano Jiménez queda fuera de las canchas tres meses por lesión en rodilla
item.description: El delantero de la selección mexicana Raúl Jiménez estará fuera de las canchas lo que resta del año debido a una lesión en la rodilla que requiere intervención quirúrgica, informó el miércoles un directivo del club Wolverhampton Wanderers de la segunda división de Inglaterra.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El delantero de la selección mexicana Raúl Jiménez estará fuera de las canchas lo que resta del año debido a una lesión en la rodilla que requiere intervención quirúrgica, informó el miércoles un directivo del club Wolverhampton Wanderers de la segunda división de Inglaterra. El jugador de 35 años se lesionó la rodilla hace cuatro semanas durante un partido de su club ante el Everton, razón por la que no fue convocado por el director técnico de la selección mexicana Rafael Márquez para los partidos de la fecha FIFA disputados entre el 26 de septiembre y el 6 de octubre. "Raúl sufrió una lesión en el ligamento colateral medial de la rodilla izquierda contra el Everton hace cuatro semanas. Lamentablemente, la lesión no ha evolucionado como esperábamos, por lo que hemos decidido que lo mejor es operar para reparar dicho ligamento", dijo el director de rendimiento de Wolverhampton Wanderers, Phil Hayward, citado en un comunicado del club. "Se someterá a la intervención este viernes en Londres y luego afrontará unos tres meses de rehabilitación antes de estar listo para volver a jugar. Es una situación realmente decepcionante para todos, pero debemos mirar hacia adelante, realizar la operación e iniciar el proceso de rehabilitación cuanto antes para que pueda regresar al campo y ayudar al equipo lo más rápido posible", agregó. Jiménez regresó en junio al Wolverhampton Wanderers después de tres años, en los que jugó para el Fulham. En su primera etapa con los "Wolves", entre 2018 y 2023, Jiménez anotó 57 goles en 166 partidos. "Raúl está muy decepcionado, pero también contento de que ahora tengamos un plan claro y definido. Podemos trabajar sobre esa base y asegurarnos de que logre recuperarse dentro de los plazos previstos", apuntó Hayward.

item.title: Cacau em Londres atinge maior cotação em um mês; café também sobe
item.description: Os futuros de cacau em Londres atingiram a maior cotação em um mês nesta quarta-feira, impulsionados por preocupações de que o tempo seco possa reduzir a produção na África Ocidental nesta safra.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os futuros de cacau em Londres atingiram a maior cotação em um mês nesta quarta-feira, impulsionados por preocupações de que o tempo seco possa reduzir a produção na África Ocidental nesta safra. CACAU * Os futuros de cacau em Londres fecharam com alta de £25, ou 0,6%, a £4.317 por tonelada, após atingir uma máxima de um mês de £4.499. * Operadores afirmaram que o tempo seco na Costa do Marfim e em partes de Gana contribuiu para a alta dos preços, intensificando as preocupações com o impacto do fenômeno climático El Niño nas safras. * Eles observaram que os dados sobre a moagem de cacau do terceiro trimestre devem ser o foco no curto prazo. Relatórios abrangendo tanto a Europa quanto a América do Norte devem ser divulgados na quinta-feira. * A moagem de cacau da Costa do Marfim subiu 46,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior em setembro, para 49.517 toneladas de grãos, segundo dados divulgados nesta quarta-feira pela associação de exportadores GEPEX. * O cacau de Nova York ficou praticamente inalterado, a US$5.735 por tonelada. CAFÉ * O do café arábica fechou em alta de 5,35 centavos, ou 1,8%, a US$2,9805 por libra-peso, a maior cotação em uma semana. * Operadores afirmaram que o mercado foi sustentado, em parte, por preocupações de que um fenômeno El Niño reduza a produção global na safra 2027/28. * A recente valorização do real brasileiro , ligada às crescentes expectativas de que Flávio Bolsonaro seja eleito presidente após sua vitória no primeiro turno, também impulsionou os preços denominados em dólares. * Um real forte reduz o incentivo para que os cafeicultores brasileiros vendam seu café, ao diminuir os preços baseados no dólar em termos de moeda local. * O café robusta subiu 0,7%, para US$3.483 por tonelada. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto fechou em queda de 0,27 centavo, ou 1,3%, a 20,84 centavos por libra-peso. * Os corretores afirmaram que o mercado perdeu o ímpeto de alta após atingir um pico de 19 meses, de 21,24 centavos, em 7 de outubro, e parecia destinado a permanecer dentro de uma faixa estreita no curto prazo. * O mercado continuou sendo sustentado pelas chuvas no Brasil, que haviam desacelerado a produção em setembro e na primeira quinzena de outubro. * O contrato de açúcar branco registrou queda de 1,2%, para US$554,90 por tonelada.

item.title: Soja recua com avanço da colheita, apesar da retomada da demanda chinesa
item.description: Os futuros de milho e soja dos Estados Unidos recuaram nesta quarta-feira, à medida que o ritmo acelerado da colheita no Meio-Oeste aumentou a oferta, com previsão de condições climáticas predominantemente favoráveis após as chuvas ocorridas no meio da semana em algumas regiões.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os futuros de milho e soja dos Estados Unidos recuaram nesta quarta-feira, à medida que o ritmo acelerado da colheita no Meio-Oeste aumentou a oferta, com previsão de condições climáticas predominantemente favoráveis após as chuvas ocorridas no meio da semana em algumas regiões. As perdas na soja foram limitadas pela notícia de que a China comprou vários carregamentos dos EUA, nas primeiras compras significativas desde uma reunião comercial de alto nível no mês passado. O trigo registrou ligeira alta devido a preocupações com a oferta da Rússia e da Ucrânia, já que ataques a navios cargueiros interromperam os embarques da região do Mar Negro. O milho e a soja continuam sustentados pela colheita em ritmo acelerado no Meio-Oeste. O Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA informou que 33% do milho e 46% da soja do país haviam sido colhidos até domingo, à medida que os agricultores aproveitaram o tempo mais seco após as chuvas terem atrasado a colheita em setembro. As chuvas desta semana paralisaram os trabalhos no campo, mas esperava-se que o tempo mais seco voltasse até o final da semana, segundo os meteorologistas. “Hoje estamos em baixa devido ao andamento do plantio e ao fato de que parece que teremos bom tempo daqui para frente. Mas estamos nos mantendo em níveis mais baixos, dentro da faixa de negociação. Os usuários finais estão intensificando as compras no mercado”, disse Jack Scoville, analista do The Price Group. Compradores do governo chinês reservaram de 8 a 10 cargas de soja dos EUA na terça-feira, informaram operadores à Reuters. O USDA confirmou a maioria das compras na quarta-feira, em um comunicado diário sobre vendas para exportação. Os operadores estão atentos a novas compras, já que a China busca cumprir um compromisso de compra anual de 25 milhões de toneladas, em meio a preocupações com o excesso de capacidade de esmagamento no país. A Administração Geral das Alfândegas da China informou uma queda de 7,7% nas importações de soja em setembro. O contrato de soja para novembro na bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) fechou com queda de 6,5 centavos, a US$12,7725 por bushel, enquanto o contrato de milho para dezembro recuou 2 centavos, para US$ 4,8075 por bushel. O trigo de dezembro da CBOT subiu 4 centavos, fechando a US$6,7325 por bushel, após a notícia de que dois navios cargueiros haviam sido atingidos por drones na costa da Bulgária.

item.title: Olympic champion Hassan withdraws from NYC Marathon
item.description: Olympic champion Sifan Hassan has dropped out of the New York City Marathon due to a setback in her training, she said on Wednesday, months after an Achilles injury forced her out of the London Marathon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Olympic champion Sifan Hassan has dropped out of the New York City Marathon due to a setback in her training, she said on Wednesday, months after an [USN:L6N40B0UW TEXT:"Achilles injury"] forced her out of the London Marathon. Hassan, who won the Paris 2024 marathon and also picked up gold in the 5,000 and 10,000 metres at the Tokyo Games, has not competed since she last ran the five boroughs a year ago, finishing sixth. "I was so excited to come back stronger, but a sickness slowed down my training and I’m not where I wanted to be," Hassan wrote on social media. "Sometimes, things just don’t go as planned." Hassan was one of two high-profile names to drop out of the year's final marathon major on Wednesday. US Olympic trials champion Fiona O'Keeffe also withdrew due to injury.

item.title: Petróleo sobe com ataques na Arábia Saudita e novas táticas do Irã para atacar petroleiros
item.description: Os preços do petróleo subiram nesta quarta-feira, depois que os houthis atacaram a sede da Saudi Aramco e o Irã afirmou que estava adotando novas táticas para atacar navios e manter os preços do petróleo elevados.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo subiram nesta quarta-feira, depois que os houthis atacaram a sede da Saudi Aramco e o Irã afirmou que estava adotando novas táticas para atacar navios e manter os preços do petróleo elevados. Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam com alta de 0,35%, a US$106,06 o barril. O petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos Estados Unidos subiu 1,01%, para US$95,09, a maior cotação em três semanas. Os ataques a navios que transitam pelo Estreito de Ormuz e os confrontos entre a Arábia Saudita e os houthis, aliados do Irã, estão elevando os preços do petróleo, disse Phil Flynn, analista sênior do Price Futures Group. “Estamos vendo muitas negociações motivadas pelo medo hoje”, acrescentou Flynn. Autoridades iranianas se recusaram a fornecer detalhes sobre a nova estratégia para atacar navios, mas uma delas afirmou que o Irã começou a usar táticas ofensivas diferentes há cerca de 10 dias. Os fluxos de petróleo do Golfo Pérsico, excluindo o Irã, dispararam em setembro para mais de 81% dos níveis pré-guerra, segundo dados, impulsionados por uma recuperação nas exportações sauditas. As exportações iranianas caíram para zero devido a um bloqueio dos Estados Unidos. “Mais petróleo chegando aos mercados internacionais não significa necessariamente que mais petróleo esteja sendo produzido”, afirmou o analista Ole Hansen, do Saxo Bank, em uma nota. “Parte da recuperação reflete uma redistribuição dos barris disponíveis, incluindo volumes que, de outra forma, teriam abastecido as refinarias regionais.” ATAQUES EM VÁRIAS FRENTES Os houthis atacaram um prédio administrativo pertencente à empresa estatal de petróleo Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) na cidade de Dhahran, causando um incêndio de pequena magnitude, informou o Ministério da Energia da Arábia Saudita. O grupo lançou mísseis balísticos e drones contra a Arábia Saudita na última semana, no que afirma ser uma retaliação ao apoio do reino às forças governamentais iemenitas. O aeroporto internacional de Riade foi atingido quatro vezes, com um ataque no sábado que matou 13 pessoas. Enquanto isso, um navio porta-contêineres afundou em águas ao sul do Estreito de Ormuz após colidir com uma mina naval e pegar fogo, informou a Marinha da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã em comunicado divulgado pela mídia estatal nesta quarta-feira. Isso ocorreu um dia depois que a Agência de Operações de Comércio Marítimo do Reino Unido informou que um navio porta-contêineres e um petroleiro foram atingidos por projéteis desconhecidos dentro do estreito. “A expectativa de que o aumento das exportações russas de diesel alivie a escassez no mercado provavelmente limitará movimentos bruscos de preço em qualquer direção”, disse Hiroyuki Kikukawa, estrategista-chefe da Nissan Securities Investment.

item.title: Mexico's Banamex markets risky debt ahead of Citi split
item.description: Mexican lender Banamex is marketing its first sale of high-risk bonds, a key move to reshape its capital structure as it prepares for independence from its parent, US banking giant Citigroup .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexican lender Banamex is marketing its first sale of high-risk bonds, a key move to reshape its capital structure as it prepares for independence from its parent, US banking giant Citigroup (C.N) . The offering of [USN:Ifp4Y5MPH TEXT:"US-dollar perpetual bonds"] - reported on Wednesday by financial publication IFR - is the latest step in Banamex's strategy to build a standalone balance sheet and broaden its international investor base. The deal follows a $1.3 billion debt sale in May, its first in decades. Citigroup has been unwinding its ownership of the Mexican bank, recently selling a 49% stake to a [USN:S0N3UB042 TEXT:"group of investors"] that includes Mexican businessman [USN:L3N3VB1D0 TEXT:"Fernando Chico Pardo"], Blackstone, and General Atlantic. Citigroup retains a 51% stake, which it is expected to sell through an [USN:L4N3ZJ1O3 TEXT:"initial public offering"] (IPO) in 2027. The "Additional Tier 1" (AT1) notes are designed to absorb losses. Investors could see their holdings written off if the bank's capital drops below a specific level. The notes are expected to receive a non-investment grade, or "junk," rating, according to the IFR report and an investor-meeting invitation seen by Reuters. Citigroup is serving as the global coordinator and active bookrunner for the deal, according to the invitation.

item.title: Eagles open practice windows for LG Landon Dickerson, 3 others
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for three-time Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson and three other players.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia Eagles opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for three-time Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson and three other players. Dickerson struggled through a knee injury in the Eagles' 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders on Sept. 13 and was placed on injured reserve the following day. Also on Wednesday, running back Saquon Barkley wasn't spotted during the portion of practice open to the media, while wide receiver DeVonta Smith was working on the JUGS machine. Both players are working their way back from hamstring injuries. As for Dickerson, his injury is separate from the knee problem that hindered him last season. Dickerson underwent surgery in August 2025 to repair a meniscus injury, then returned to start 15 games, later acknowledging he came back before he was fully recovered. Dickerson, 28, has started all but one of the 79 games in which he has appeared since being selected by the Eagles in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft. The Eagles also opened the 21-day practice windows for defensive back Jakorian Bennett and tight ends Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers on Wednesday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Goolsbee de la Fed afirma que datos del IPC de septiembre fueron desalentadores: Yahoo Finance
item.description: El presidente del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmó el miércoles que los últimos datos sobre la inflación al consumo le tenían preocupado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmó el miércoles que los últimos datos sobre la inflación al consumo le tenían preocupado. Los datos del índice de precios al consumo de septiembre, que mostraron presiones sobre los precios superiores a lo esperado, eran "desalentadores", afirmó Goolsbee en una entrevista con Yahoo Finance. En lo que respecta a los datos sobre la presión de los precios, "me preocupa, no solo la cifra global, sino que, si se desglosan los componentes, la inflación de los servicios muestra pocos signos de mejora", señaló el responsable, al tiempo que afirmó que el banco central volverá a situar la inflación en su objetivo del 2 %.

item.title: Ocho estados de EEUU demandan a OpenAI, alegando que ChatGPT perjudica a los niños
item.description: Iowa, Kansas y otros seis estados anunciaron el miércoles que habían demandado a OpenAI en tribunales por los daños que, dicen, ChatGPT ha causado a los niños, alegando que el chatbot ha incitado a los niños a hacerse daño a sí mismos o a otros.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Iowa, Kansas y otros seis estados anunciaron el miércoles que habían demandado a OpenAI en tribunales por los daños que, dicen, ChatGPT ha causado a los niños, alegando que el chatbot ha incitado a los niños a hacerse daño a sí mismos o a otros. Las demandas, presentadas ante tribunales estatales, solicitan una orden que obligue a OpenAI a modificar el funcionamiento de ChatGPT en lo que respecta a los menores. Los estados también solicitan una orden que obligue a la empresa a renunciar a los beneficios que ha obtenido gracias a los usuarios jóvenes. El fiscal general de Florida fue el primero en demandar a OpenAI, presentando en junio una demanda por motivos similares. La empresa también se enfrenta a decenas de demandas en las que se alega que ChatGPT ha contribuido a tiroteos masivos y otros actos violentos.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee says September CPI data was discouraging - Yahoo Finance
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Wednesday the latest consumer-level inflation data left him worried about the state of price pressures.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Wednesday the latest consumer-level inflation data left him worried about the state of price pressures. The September [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer price index"] data, which showed higher-than-expected price pressures, was “discouraging,” Goolsbee said in an interview with Yahoo Finance. When it comes to the price pressure data, “I'm concerned, related to not just the overall number, but if you break out the components, services inflation shows little sign of improvement,” the official said, while affirming the central bank will get inflation back to its 2% target. Goolsbee stopped short of saying how he thinks the central bank should respond with rate policy in the near term while saying in strong terms that the Fed can't allow high price pressures to persist. If inflation pressures remain elevated, "there's not ambiguity about what, how the central bank has to deal with that," he said. "You must prevent the buildup of overheating, because if you get overheating buildup on the demand side, that tends to be very persistent and hard to get rid of," Goolsbee said. The Fed raised its interest rate target by a quarter percentage point last month to between 3.75% and 4% and penciled in an additional increase by the end of the year, as it works to get inflation to its 2% target. Key Fed officials have [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"waved"] markets off expectations of a rate hike at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting set for the end of the month, though the release of the CPI data put new life into market expectations that the central bank may move again sooner rather than later. In the interview, Goolsbee explained that the inflation data showed that price pressures are high even in the areas outside those directly impacted by things like tariffs, which is in part why he found the latest report to be so vexing. "This month's reading is over 5% for services inflation and you can't really attribute services inflation to tariffs, to oil prices, or things like that," Goolsbee said. "On the ground here in the Midwest, everywhere we're going, we're hearing about costs and we're hearing about prices," Goolsbee said. "There's very little that we're hearing that sounds like downturn, risks of recession and things like that, so that makes you more nervous about demand side overheating than just straight supply shock." The Fed has failed to get inflation back to its 2% target for over five years, though officials say market and public expectations data shows continued confidence that price pressures will be brought under control.

item.title: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?
item.description: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted military-grade Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"SpaceX had restricted "military-grade" Starlink services"], hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses. The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield, a military version developed for the Pentagon. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company." WHAT IS STARLINK? Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX (SPCX.O) , is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions. WHAT IS STARSHIELD? Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon. While its missions are separate from Starlink's commercial broadband service, the distinction is not always clear-cut: Starshield's secure communications services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone. Starshield leverages the technology, engineering and operational experiences of Starlink, according to SpaceX. In addition to secure communications, the company says the militarized version can also provide users with Earth observation and the ability to integrate sensors or other payloads. The Pentagon, Starshield's largest customer, has spent billions of dollars on both Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024. Questions over the relationship between Starlink and Starshield have persisted since [USN:L1N31S38K TEXT:"Russia threatened Western satellites supporting Ukraine in 2022"]. SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque. Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the [USN:L6N41W1B2 TEXT:"Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services"] used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal. [USN:L6N4290XG TEXT:"Britain has also adopted Starshield"]. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters. Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. New Zealand is doing a trial of Starshield to assess its usefulness for military operations, the New Zealand Defence Force previously told Reuters.

SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque. Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal. Britain has also adopted Starshield. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters. Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. New Zealand is doing a trial of Starshield to assess its usefulness for military operations, the New Zealand Defence Force previously told Reuters.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Former portfolio manager sues Fidelity after leaving for Michael Dell's family office
item.description: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell. The suit, filed by Adam Benjamin in the Suffolk Division of the Superior Court of Massachusetts, alleges that after Fidelity executives failed to persuade him to stay at the firm, the company "turned on a dime" and terminated him on July 10 of this year. Fidelity then imposed a non-compete clause, causing him to forfeit a compensation package totaling in the millions of dollars. "Rather than protecting any legitimate business interests, the provisions are being broadly misused by Fidelity as a retention tool or improper barrier/deterrent to" Benjamin's ability to pursue other professional opportunities, the lawsuit alleges. Fidelity declined to comment on the lawsuit, which was filed on Friday. Neither Benjamin nor his lawyers could be reached for comment. Non-compete agreements are common in the asset management industry. Benjamin managed the $48 billion Fidelity Select Semiconductors Portfolio, which is up 58% so far this year, compared to 13.3% for the S&P 500 (.SPX) index. Its average annual return of 37.4% over the last five years puts it in the top percentile of all comparable funds rated by Morningstar, which awarded the fund five stars and a gold medalist rating, its top score. Benjamin began working at DFO on October 1, the lawsuit said. He alleged that Fidelity's withholding of compensation rests on the false claim that he was joining a competitor. He said he has never worked for Fidelity's own family office business.

item.title: US judge won't block Trump order targeting DEI by federal contractors
item.description: A federal judge declined on Wednesday to block an effort by President Donald Trump to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives by companies that do business with the US government.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: A federal judge declined on Wednesday to block an effort by President Donald Trump to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives by companies that do business with the US government. US District Judge Adam Abelson in Baltimore, Maryland, said that groups representing university faculty and minority business owners had failed to show [USN:L1N40S0IR TEXT:"a March executive order"] by the Republican president was too broad. Trump's order bars [USN:FWN40E0ZQ TEXT:""racially discriminatory DEI activities""] by federal contractors and requires them to certify their compliance in writing. Businesses that do not comply could lose contracts and be investigated for violating the federal False Claims Act. The groups in their lawsuit claim that Trump's order wrongly presumes that all DEI amounts to illegal racial discrimination and extends to speech protected by the US Constitution. But Abelson said its definition of unlawful conduct was narrower. "The Contractors Order only prohibits contractors from engaging in conduct that is already prohibited by federal law: intentional discrimination on the basis of race or ethnicity," wrote Abelson, an appointee of President Joe Biden , a Democrat. The judge denied the groups' motion to block Trump's order pending the outcome of the lawsuit, which was filed in April. The plaintiffs are represented by Democracy Forward, a progressive legal group. In a statement, the group said the decision would be reassuring for federal contractors because it made clear that Trump's order does not broadly prohibit diversity programs. “And the court confirmed that order reaches no further than the work a contractor performs for the government on the specific contract where the language appears," the group said. The US Department of Justice did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Trump's order is also being challenged by 19 Democratic-led states and Washington, DC, in [USN:L1N42I0ZX TEXT:"a lawsuit in the same court"]. That case seeks to block federal agencies from altering contracts to comply with Trump's order. Many of the largest US businesses, from defense and tech companies to food service providers and logistics firms, are federal contractors, and some companies primarily depend on the government for work. Civil rights advocates say DEI practices help address historic inequities for marginalized groups like women, LGBTQ people and ethnic minorities. But Trump and many conservatives cast DEI [USN:L8N42O1L3 TEXT:"as anti-merit and discriminatory"] against groups like white people and men, and his administration has moved to eradicate it from government, higher education and the private sector. Trump has [USN:L1N3Z20XX TEXT:"banned DEI programs by federal agencies"] and repealed a 1965 executive order requiring federal contractors to take affirmative action to hire minorities and women.

item.title: As Ukraine struggles with Starlink and US satellite data, Europe has no quick fix
item.description: As Ukraine reported problems with Starlink satellite internet terminals and US data that warns of Russian ballistic missile attacks, Kyiv also faced the harsh reality that its European allies cannot offer any ready-made alternatives.
item.dc:creator: Vaishnavi Hajari, Gianluca Lo Nostro, Cassell Bryan-Low
item.content:encoded: As Ukraine [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"reported problems"] with Starlink satellite internet terminals and US data that warns of Russian ballistic missile attacks, Kyiv also faced the harsh reality that its European allies cannot offer any ready-made alternatives. Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday the functioning of Starlink’s military-grade service Starshield had been interrupted when terminals were moving at high speed, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defence. Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that, for the second night running, Ukraine had received no warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv. The reasons for the difficulties were not immediately clear but followed another souring of relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukraine, after Trump announced a deal to waive sanctions on Russian diesel and called for Zelenskiy to be replaced. Trump said on Tuesday that the US was still sharing intelligence with Ukraine. Elon Musk and his SpaceX company had no immediate comment on Ukraine’s assertions. European countries have voiced strong support for Ukraine and Zelenskiy. But the problems with vital data highlighted that Ukraine and Europe depend heavily on US systems for both low-orbit satellite communications — provided by SpaceX via Starlink — and space-based infrared sensing that feeds into early-warning systems. A US satellite constellation called the Space-Based Infrared System provides early missile warnings. “That is fairly unique and … what basically that can detect is the heat generated by missiles as they're launched,” said Marc DeVore, an associate fellow at think tank Chatham House. “There is nothing equivalent in Europe.” NO SIMPLE STARLINK SWAP FOR UKRAINE, EUROPE As for Starlink, Europe does not have a ready-made alternative that Ukrainian soldiers could attach to their drones, although European governments and companies are working on long-term options. Shares in European satellite operator Eutelsat [USN:L6N4600QK TEXT:"soared"] on Wednesday following news of Ukraine's difficulties with Starshield, fuelled by investor bets that European providers could benefit from growing strains between Washington and Kyiv. But Christian Freiherr von der Ropp, an independent satellite consultant, said Eutelsat's OneWeb network was [USN:L5N3PN1Q8 TEXT:"not well suited"] to wartime use. "Its current constellation remains rooted in an outdated architecture and technology conceived a decade ago, without any evolution of its underlying design," he said. "Capacity and performance constraints, combined with the cost, weight, bulk and power consumption of its user terminals, limit its suitability for frontline applications." A spokesperson for Eutelsat told Reuters that the company continued to provide connectivity services in Ukraine through its low Earth orbit and geostationary orbit networks with its partners. It declined to comment further "given the sensitive nature of the situation." Von der Ropp also said switching networks would require replacing thousands of terminals, as Starlink and Starshield terminals use proprietary technology and could not simply connect to OneWeb. Bohdan Sas, co-founder of Ukrainian defence technology startup Buntar Aerospace, said the sudden interruption to Starshield services "highlights to almost every end user both in Ukraine and abroad you can’t rely solely on one solution that can be switched off.” “You need to have some kind of sovereign capabilities," he added, so that "you are not subject to somebody’s mood today.” Fears of over-reliance on US defence technology have grown in Europe in recent years, as Trump has threatened to quit the NATO military alliance just as European leaders see Russia posing the greatest threat to the continent in decades. European Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said at a conference hosted by Politico in Brussels on Wednesday that the continent was "quite dependent on American space capabilities.” “The answer to that situation is to develop our own capabilities,” he added, mentioning the European Union's planned satellite constellation IRIS² and urging European countries to work together. But that project is years from becoming operational even if everything goes according to plan, causing frustration among European government officials. Germany is developing its own military satellite constellation.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（14日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
上昇して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反発。米インフレ指標を受けてポンドが対ドルで下落したこ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（14日） 3:54 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

上昇して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反発。米インフレ指標を受けてポンドが対ドルで下落したことが好感され、輸出関連株が買われた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数も０．０９％高と続伸した。

製薬大手アストラゼネカは３．４％、ＧＳＫは３．６％、それぞれ上昇した。

英日用品のユニリーバは２．５％、高級ブランド会社バーバリーは３．５％いずれも値上がりした。

ヒーリー英財務相は、予算案に盛り込む新施策に関し、国債発行には依存せず、増税もしくは歳出削減によって財源を確保する見通しだと報じられた。

イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）チーフエコノミストのピル氏は、市場で今後１年間に４回の利上げが見込まれていることに懐疑的な見方を示した。これを受けて、ＦＴＳＥ３５０種住宅建設株指数は３．２３％上昇。

一方、金などの値下がりで貴金属株指数 は３．５３％安。銀行株指数 は０．５８％下落した。

９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月からの伸び率が加速し、市場予想を上回った。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

小幅に反発して取引を終えた。半導体関連企業による強気な需要見通しを受け、人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る懸念が和らいだ。

２０２６年７─９月期決算を発表したオランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは１．２％高。２９、３０年の発注に向けて顧客から関心が寄せられていると明らかにし、需要が堅調に推移する見通しが示された。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種ヘルスケア株指数は２．３１％高。ベルギーでの人員削減を発表した製薬大手ＧＳＫは３．６％上昇した。

一方、資源株指数は１．１８％安。ＪＰモルガンが目標株価を引き下げた貴金属採掘フレスニヨは４．６％下落した。

デンマークの風力発電大手オーステッドは３．９％安。米国の洋上風力発電所事業への懸念から、売られた。スウェーデンの銀行ＳＥＢは４．６％安。

ブレント原油先物価格は高値圏で推移。インフレへの懸念から、市場は欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が１２月会合で追加利上げに踏み切るとの観測を強めている。

また、９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月からの伸び率が加速し、市場予想を上回った。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが上昇した。米国のインフレ加速で連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測が強まり、米債利回りが上昇した動きに追随した。

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速し、１０月中の米利上げの可能性が再び意識される状況となった。

クインテット・プライベート・バンクのチーフストラテジスト、ダニエレ・アントヌッチ氏は「総合とコアの双方でインフレが加速したことは、物価上昇圧力の持続性が強まっていることを示唆する」と指摘。「堅調な成長と相まって、これはわれわれがＦＲＢが年内の追加利上げに踏み切ると予想する理由の一つだ」と述べた。

米国経済の規模と重要性、ＦＲＢが他の中央銀行に及ぼす影響力を踏まえると、米金融政策を巡る見通しは他の世界の債券市場にも影響を与える傾向がある。

米ＣＰＩを受けて米債券利回りが上昇する中、ドイツ１０年債利回りもこれに追随し、２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．４８１％となった。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約１４０ｂｐ。１０月序盤には一時１５８ｂｐ超まで拡大していた。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１４日、フランスは財政健全化を通じて自国の債務問題を解決すべきだと述べ、ＥＣＢによる債券市場への介入観測を事実上けん制した。

ＥＣＢは今年、２５ｂｐの利上げを２回実施している。短期金融市場は１２月の理事会までに追加利上げが実施されるとの見方を完全に織り込んでいる。

item.title: US stocks: AI shares tumble, erasing $80 billion as hot US inflation fuels rate fears
item.description: Amid rising inflation, major AI firms like CoreWeave and Dell Technologies experienced significant stock price drops, losing around $80 billion in market value. Increased US interest rates have investors worried about the borrowing hurdles faced by less profitable firms within the sector. Even with the strong performance of giants like Nvidia and Microsoft, skepticism remains high, reminiscent of the dot-com era's cautionary tales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.Among the leading decliners were data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, off 11%, cloud computing giant Oracle, down 9%, and AI server seller Dell Technologies, down 11%. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value.The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year - part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations.Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%. We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave, said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners.Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting irrationally and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates.Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia to the so-called hyperscalers - primarily Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon - are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt.But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63% before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon. I do think long rates above 5% and creeping towards 6% is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them, said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers. The Nasdaq was down 2% on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2%. SpaceX, another major AI player, was down 3%. I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon, said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. Those five are spending like 75% of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good. Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000. This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds, Ellerbroek said. Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective.

item.title: PSG down Man City 4-2 in pulsating Champions League clash
item.description: Twice-defending champions Paris St Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Twice-defending champions Paris St Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny. On a breathless night featuring 46 goals, Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool's 6-3 thrashing of LASK, Aston Villa recorded the biggest European victory in their history with a 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce and Real Madrid staged a stunning late comeback to beat AS Roma 4-3. But no fixture carried more intrigue than the Etihad clash, where City played their first home game since being found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules. City, who have denied all wrongdoing and appealed the verdict, were carved open by PSG in the first half. PSG'S FIRST-HALF BLITZ Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele scored less than two minutes apart before Warren Zaire-Emery's clever touch released Vitinha to drive the third beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 32nd minute. City emerged transformed after the break and Erling Haaland headed in Iliman Ndiaye's cross in the 53rd minute to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the landmark in 60 games compared with Lionel Messi’s previous record of 80. City's joy was short-lived as Maghnes Akliouche's stunning long-range strike found the net despite Donnarumma getting a hand to it. Haaland had the City fans on their feet when he swept home Ayyoub Bouaddi's pass in the 75th minute for his second, before Donnarumma made up for his blunder by saving a penalty from Ferran Torres. The match unfolded against an "us against the world" backdrop, with City fans in the South Stand holding up cards that read "CTID" (City Till I Die). Former City manager Pep Guardiola watched from the stands alongside chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and senior executives Ferran Soriano and Hugo Viana. VILLA HIT FENERBAHCE FOR SIX At Villa Park, Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both scored twice in a dominant display by the hosts. Johan Manzambi opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Jackson struck in the 31st and 39th minutes to give Villa a commanding halftime lead. Barkley added a fourth from the penalty spot in the 68th minute before grabbing his second four minutes later, while Tammy Abraham completed the rout with a stoppage-time strike. At the Stadio Olimpico, Real Madrid scored three times in the closing stages to overturn a two-goal deficit. Marten de Roon gave Roma the lead in the 20th minute before Kylian Mbappe equalised five minutes later, but Donyell Malen struck twice in the 51st and 57th minutes to put the hosts in control. However, the visitors mounted a remarkable comeback as Carlos Espi pulled a goal back in the 82nd minute before Endrick levelled three minutes later. Former Roma defender Antonio Ruediger then completed the turnaround in the 90th minute, holding off his marker to steer home Arda Guler's inswinging corner from close range and snatch victory for the Spanish side. Liverpool's Barcola, meanwhile, scored his first goals for the club with his hat-trick in their rout of Champions League newcomers LASK in Austria. Ronald Araujo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also scored for Andoni Iraola's side, who bounced back from Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by City. Florian Flecker struck twice for the hosts.

item.title: 燃料高で物価圧力強まる、雇用は横ばい傾向＝米地区連銀報告
item.description: [１４日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１４日発表した地区連銀経済報告（ベージュブック）で、米国の労働市場...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
燃料高で物価圧力強まる、雇用は横ばい傾向＝米地区連銀報告 3:46 配信

２０１９年３月撮影　REUTERS/Leah Millis

[１４日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１４日発表した地区連銀経済報告（ベージュブック）で、米国の労働市場は雇用も解雇も低水準にとどまる状態が続く一方、一部地域でインフレ圧力が強まっていることが示された。

地区連銀経済報告は「企業はディーゼル燃料（軽油）価格の高止まりを報告し、燃料サーチャージを通じてコスト上昇がサプライチェーン全体に転嫁されていると指摘した」と報告。物価動向について、１２地区連銀のうち３地区で全般的な価格上昇が「力強い」と報告され、８地区は「緩やか」と報告された。

雇用については、大半の地区で全体的な雇用水準にほとんど、もしくは全く変化がみられなかったと報告した。

全般的な経済活動は、２地区で「緩やかな」ペースで成長。３地区は「控えめ」なペース、４地区は「小幅な」成長を報告し、３地区では経済活動に大きな変化は見られなかった。国内の多くの地域で企業が景気見通しについて前向きな見方を維持していると報告されたが、「成長見通しは概して小幅なものにとどまり、製造業がけん引する一方で、根強い不確実性が重しとなっている」とした。

インフレが広範囲に波及するとの懸念が高まる中、軽油価格の高騰に関する言及は２１件だった。前回の報告の２件から大幅に増加した。ダラス地区連銀は「コスト上昇の要因として最も多く挙がったのが軽油で、貨物輸送や農業、航空運賃に影響し、多くの産業で利益率を圧迫している」と指摘した。複数の地区で「その他のコモディティー（商品）や関税、保険による価格圧力も続いている」との指摘もあった。

複数の地区連銀は大規模な解雇は見られないとしたが、５地区では退職者の補充見送りや採用手控えで人員を削減していると報告。いくつかの地区では、個人からの生活費上昇への対応や、福利厚生の拡充といった形でインフレが賃金上昇圧力となっていると報告された。

労働市場に対する人工知能（ＡＩ）の影響も示され、シカゴ地区連銀では、ＡＩ導入による生産性の向上に伴う雇用の削減が報告された。一方、ダラス地区連銀の人材派遣会社は、ＡＩ導入拡大を管理するために採用担当者を新規雇用したという。

住宅市場の低調も顕著になっており、フィラデルフィア地区連銀は「中古住宅販売は引き続き小幅に減少した」と報告。「９月の住宅ローン金利上昇により、住宅市場の活動はさらに鈍化した。借入コストの上昇で希望者が購入を手控える一方、売り出し物件の在庫は低水準にとどまっている」という。ニューヨーク地区連銀は、金利上昇が市場への住宅供給を抑制していると指摘。

ボストンやニューヨーク、ミネアポリス、サンフランシスコの各連銀では、悪化したカナダとの貿易関係も製造業や観光業の抑制要因として挙げられた。

今回の報告は１０月５日までに収集された情報に基づき、フィラデルフィア地区連銀が作成した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 〔アングル〕ＥＵの自動車現地調達ルール案、中国勢は先回りで足場固め コラム：「ウォール街」と実体経済の温度差、ＡＩブームで一層鮮明に アングル：金価格、米国債利回り上昇でも4000ドル台維持　中銀の準備資産分散が下支え アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず 最終更新: 10/15(木) 6:32 ロイター

item.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
item.description: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others. Attorneys general from the states, which include Iowa, Kansas and Arizona, filed the lawsuits independently in state courts, claiming ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to earn the trust of users. But the chatbot reinforces delusions, encourages dangerous behavior and assists users in planning violence like mass shootings, the lawsuits claim. The lawsuits represent the most significant coordinated state action against an artificial intelligence company, adding to a wave of legal challenges OpenAI faces as it prepares for a public listing. Florida's attorney general filed the first such state [USN:L6N429106 TEXT:"suit"] in June. The lawsuits accuse the company of violating state consumer protection laws by misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT. The states also allege that the company created a public nuisance by endangering the health of their residents. The lawsuits seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works. Among other things, the states want the company barred from developing AI models that can improve themselves unless it can ensure those models are aligned with human values. The states, which also include Arkansas, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia, are also seeking civil monetary penalties for OpenAI's violations of state law as well as damages. A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The company is also facing dozens of lawsuits by private plaintiffs, alleging ChatGPT helped users [USN:L6N45D0ZP TEXT:"plan mass shootings"] or other violence.

item.title: Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
item.description: The diagnosis has raised concerns about the 71-year-old pontiff’s health and the future of his papacy, though the Vatican says his recovery is progressing well.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis

The diagnosis has raised concerns about the 71-year-old pontiff’s health and the future of his papacy, though the Vatican says his recovery is progressing well.

Pope Leo arrives at Gemelli Hospital ahead of the pontiff's surgery to remove a lung nodule in Rome, Italy, on Oct 13, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Guglielmo Mangiapane)

FAST

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo 's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday (Oct 14), after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer . World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Pope Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday. Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy. The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness.

Pope Leo normally follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17 and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip. However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the amount of time his recovery would take. The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world 's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

PRAYERS FOR POPE LEO A prayer was recited for Pope Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery. The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer , and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancer ous tissue. Human lung s have five lobes - three in the right lung and two in the left. The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope 's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone, said late on Tuesday. The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis. Dr Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Pope Leo 's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment. "If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed." Pope Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had recent health issues.

Related:

What we know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo recovering after lung cancer operation

ENGAGEMENTS CANCELLED UNTIL NEXT WEEK The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until Oct 20. The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act of an assembly of bishops called by Pope Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders so far during this papacy. Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Pope Leo . The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role. Political leaders offered messages of support. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope , an American who was born in Chicago. "May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," he said on X. Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican in May. There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope , or from Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 14 : Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.Among the leading decliners were data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16 per cent, AI infra

Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 14 : Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector. Among the leading decliners were data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16 per cent, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, off 11 per cent, cloud computing giant Oracle, down 9 per cent, and AI server seller Dell Technologies, down 11 per cent. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value.  The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year — part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations. Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625 per cent recently yielded 15 per cent.

"We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners.  Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates. Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia to the so-called hyperscalers — primarily Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon — are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt.  But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63 per cent before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon. "I do think long rates above 5 per cent and creeping towards 6 per cent is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. "It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers."  The Nasdaq was down 2 per cent on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2 per cent. SpaceX, another major AI player, was down 3 per cent. "I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. "Those five are spending like 75 per cent of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good." Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000. "This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds," Ellerbroek said. "Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Racial employment gap widened among new US lawyers, study finds
item.description: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show. More than 94% of 2025’s white law graduates found jobs within 10 months, compared to less than 91% of law graduates of color, according to figures released Wednesday by the National Association for Law Placement. Black law graduates had the lowest employment rate at 87%, down from nearly 90% in 2024, the NALP data showed. The employment rate for 2025 Hispanic law graduates was slightly over 91%, down from more than 92% the previous year. The employment rate for Asian law graduates held steady at about 92%. The relatively small cohort of Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander law graduates posted the highest employment rate at more than 96%. “A law degree should open doors, but NALP's latest report shows that those doors are not equally open to everyone,” NALP Executive Director Nikia Gray said in a statement after releasing the data. The law graduates of 2025 hit the job market amid the Trump administration’s widespread campaign to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion programs in higher education, government and the private sector. In March 2025, the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission [USN:L1N3Q010H TEXT:"demanded detailed hiring data from 20 major firms"], including applicant names and whether race or gender influenced their employment decisions. The US Federal Trade Commission earlier this year [USN:FWN3YV125 TEXT:"warned"] 42 major law firms that their hiring practices may violate federal antitrust law. Diversity Lab, a group that promoted diversity goals at law firms, [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"shuttered"] in June after coming under FTC scrutiny. Many major law firms have publicly withdrawn or altered their public references to diversity, equity and inclusion since Trump returned to the White House, a Reuters special report found . Nearly 50 US law firms that previously provided NALP with demographic data about their lawyers [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"declined to do so"] this year, with NALP attributing the drop to Trump’s crackdown on law firm DEI efforts. Additionally, the US Department of Education is [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"poised to revoke"] the American Bar Association’s status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools, partly because it says the ABA took too long to eliminate DEI standards for schools. According to the new NALP data, white law graduates outpaced every racial group except for Middle Eastern or North African law graduates in securing jobs that require passing the bar — considered the gold standard for legal employment. First-generation college students had a lower employment rate than law graduates whose parents attended college or law school. Read more: [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"Facing DEI pressures, some law firms shield data in latest diversity survey"] [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"Law firm diversity group shutters amid Trump's DEI crackdown"]

item.title: Lamar Jackson day-to-day, Ravens hopeful he's ready for Browns
item.description: Lamar Jackson was not made available to media for his typical Wednesday afternoon interview session and didn't practice, but signs point to the Ravens having their starting quarterback on the field Sunday against the Browns.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson was not made available to media for his typical Wednesday afternoon interview session and didn't practice, but signs point to the Ravens having their starting quarterback on the field Sunday against the Browns. "It's definitely day-to-day," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday. "A lot of times those things right when they happen you're not sure. As you gather information, you look at stuff. Again, to Lamar's credit, he's working his butt off. He's doing everything he can to be out here. And when he's able to be, he will." Ravens outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson was back at practice and is expected to be available Sunday. Jackson was not on the field at the start of Wednesday's practice, but he regularly has been idle for the first workout of the week in past seasons. Jackson missed Week 5 recovering from an ankle injury that knocked him out of Baltimore's Week 4 win over the Titans in the first half. Tyler Huntley guided Baltimore to a win at Atlanta in Jackson's absence and will continue to take some reps with the starters this week. If he's able to suit up, Jackson will be going head-to-head with former Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken. The current Browns head coach said Wednesday he is preparing "for the Ravens" more than he's planning to stop Jackson. Monken did note the Ravens are slightly harder to defend at the moment with Jackson taking more snaps under center. Without a preset launch point in the pocket, defenses have to account for every angle with Jackson and be ready for bulldozing running back Derrick Henry to come straight downhill. Jackson did not practice last week but head coach Jesse Minter said the Ravens anticipated a shorter-term recovery period. Last week, Minter left the door open for Jackson to play even without practicing. --Field Level Media

AI-powered stock funds bet bots can pick stocks faster and better than humans

FAST

PROVIDENCE, Rhode Island, Oct 14 : A handful of fund managers are betting that exchange traded funds run by AI stock-picking models can crunch data quicker and make better investment decisions than humans, even as many people remain wary or even fearful of artificial intelligence. So far, fewer than half-a-dozen ETFs, collectively managing only about $30 million of the ETF industry's nearly $17 trillion in assets, rely solely on AI-powered bots to control everything from research to stock selection. While that represents a tiny fraction of the industry, AI is making its way slowly and steadily into the investment processes of most asset managers, to some extent, even if that may not yet be visible to investors themselves. Earlier this year, 91 per cent of asset managers surveyed by Mercer reported plans to increase their use of AI-based portfolio management tools this year and said they are trying to figure out what tasks can be safely handed off to AI.      The performance of the handful of funds that rely solely on AI to generate returns shows they are beating the market, even if their track records stretch back only a few months. Their managers argue these returns will attract more investments into the idea over time.

"Until now you've had two choices: be a passive investor and own an index, or be an active investor" with a human picking stocks, said Tal Schwartz, founder and CEO of Ai Funds. "I want to offer a third option: where it's AI that is doing it all for you."  In August, Schwartz launched the High Conviction US Equity AI-Managed ETF, built on a proprietary AI learning algorithm that analyzes decades of market data. So far, it has attracted less than $20 million in assets, according to data from ETF.com, but Schwartz said it is still early days. AI can crunch more data more rapidly than any human being, he said, and strips human emotions and cognitive biases out of the investment process.  "I know this is a long-term process, that people will only become convinced over time," he added. "I think that what will convince them is performance." Schwartz's fund is up 2.7 per cent since its August 21 launch, beating the 1.1 per cent gain for the S&P 500 index in the same time frame. Two funds launched by Israeli asset manager FinQ in February have handily beaten the 11.0 per cent gain by the S&P over that time frame. FinQ's dollar-neutral US Large-Cap AI-managed ETF has soared 25.35 per cent and the version of the ETF not offering a currency hedge is 23.98 per cent higher since inception. Two other funds, the Pacer S&P 500 3AI Top 100 ETF and the Pacer S&P World 3AI Top 100 ETF, are ahead 10.34 per cent and 10.33 per cent, respectively, since their launches in early May, compared to a gain of 5.8 per cent for the S&P 500. Nonetheless, advisers and analysts said the funds' short track records and above-average fees may limit investor interest.  "Advisers are comfortable with AI that informs a decision and uneasy with AI that makes it," said Jeff Judge, a financial adviser at Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland, adding his clients are not clamoring for this. "Proof that this approach works will really come down to who can thoughtfully manage risk and ride out a down market," said Todd Sohn, ETF analyst at Strategas. AI-ENHANCED ETFS MORE COMMON Other firms have rolled out "AI-enhanced" ETFs, which use AI to undertake quantitative analysis, analyze stocks or monitor risk. This cautious approach is more common, insiders said. "We've been training models using AI for seven or eight years now, and using them to run live capital for about four years," said David Wright, head of quantitative investments at Pictet Asset Management in Geneva. His firm launched the Pictet AI Enhanced US Equity ETF in February. Since its debut, the fund has attracted $163 million in assets and posted gains of 14.8 per cent, compared to 11.4 per cent for the S&P 500. Wright compares using AI in the investment process to using a plane's autopilot functions. The autopilot may be able to take off, cruise and land with no humans involved, but, he added, "I wouldn't go on a plane that didn't have a pilot." Other asset managers are taking a similarly cautious approach to integrating AI.  "I'm not losing any sleep over robots ending the world," said Dan Taylor, deputy chief investment officer of systematic within Man Group, referring to recent headlines. "But I still do worry about AI's ability to deal with the most extreme, unlikely events, where all the action happens, both good and bad."

Source: Reuters
